acceptance_criteria.criterion: JsonObjectNode has a mandatory (not optional) JsonObject.Input("value") — it requires a sub-object to nest.
JsonObjectNode deep-copies the value input (copy.deepcopy(value)) before inserting it into the accumulating dict, preventing mutation in fork scenarios.
JsonObjectNode uses node_id="Mistralys_JsonObject", display_name="JSON Object", category="json".
JsonObjectNode outputs JSON_OBJECT, VALUE (passthrough of nested object), and KEY (passthrough of key string).
JsonToStringNode serializes using json.dumps(json_object, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False).
JsonToStringNode passes through the original json_object unchanged as the JSON_OBJECT output.
JsonToStringNode outputs the serialized string as the STRING output.
JsonToStringNode uses node_id="Mistralys_JsonToString", display_name="JSON to String", category="json".

summary: Implemented JsonObjectNode with mandatory JsonObject value input, double deep-copy (json_object and value), _set_nested_key, NodeOutput(obj, value, key).
Implemented JsonToStringNode with json.dumps(indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) and JSON_OBJECT passthrough.

comments.note: nodes.py: JsonToStringNode passes json_object through as-is (same object reference) rather than a deep copy. This is correct — the node is read-only (serialize only, no mutation) so returning the original reference is safe and avoids an unnecessary copy allocation.

Edge cases: dot-notation sub-object nesting, overwrite, empty dict, unicode, and fork-safety with two concurrent consumers.

comments.note: All 8 acceptance criteria verified. No issues found. JsonToStringNode correctly passes through the original json_object reference (same object, not a copy) — this is correct as the node is read-only, so no defensive copy needed.

Fork safety verified via edge case: two downstream consumers of the same JsonObjectNode VALUE output — deep-copy ensures neither consumer mutates the shared input, and both receive independently correct results.

JsonToStringNode is read-only — safe to pass json_object reference through unchanged.
All 8 acceptance criteria confirmed met. No blocking issues, no Fix-Forward changes needed.

comments.note: nodes.py JsonObjectNode.execute(): VALUE passthrough returns the original 'value' reference, while the deep-copy is embedded only inside the dict (via _set_nested_key). This is the correct design — VALUE is 'the exact input unchanged', and the nested dict copy is isolated from downstream VALUE mutations. Intentional and sound.

[documentation-forward] JsonObjectNode description 'Nest the values of a JSON object into the specified key.' is slightly ambiguous — 'the values' could imply multiple values being iterated. A clearer phrasing: 'Nest a JSON sub-object under the specified key.' Also lacks mention of dot-notation key support, consistent with the documentation-forward raised in WP-002.
